lesson.intro: Parafrasa menyatakan ide yang sama dengan kata dan susunan kalimat yang berbeda. Kemampuan ini penting untuk memahami bacaan, karena soal sering memakai kata lain untuk menanyakan makna yang sama.

sections.heading: Sinonim dan konteks
sections.bodyMd: Sebuah **synonym** tidak selalu cocok di semua kalimat. Kata **substitute** bisa menjadi pengganti, tetapi harus sesuai konteks. Dua kata yang **equivalent** atau **comparable** belum tentu **identical** dalam setiap situasi.

sections.heading: Parafrasa yang baik
sections.bodyMd: Parafrasa yang baik tidak hanya **replace** beberapa kata. Penulis harus memahami ide, lalu **express** ulang dengan susunan baru. Kamu juga bisa **rephrase** kalimat untuk menjelaskan ulang dengan kata sendiri.

sections.heading: Mengecek klaim
sections.bodyMd: Pilihan **alternative** yang baik tetap menjaga klaim asli. Jika klaimnya berubah, itu bukan **paraphrase** yang benar, meskipun kalimatnya terdengar halus.

block3.title: Parafrasa yang Baik
block3.text:
Paraphrase means to express the same idea in different words. Writers do this to avoid repeating themselves and to show that they understand a source. A good paraphrase keeps the meaning identical, but it replaces the original words with a synonym and changes the sentence structure. For example, 'The museum closed early' can be rephrased as 'The museum shut its doors ahead of schedule.' Both sentences give the same information, yet the second one uses different vocabulary.

A paraphrase is not the same as changing one or two words. If a writer keeps the original order and swaps a few words, the result may still look copied. Good paraphrasing requires the writer to understand the idea first, then explain it in a new way. Many students use a dictionary to find an alternative for each word. This method can work, but it often produces awkward sentences.

Some words have an equivalent in another language, while others are only comparable in meaning. A substitute word may fit one context and fail in another. For this reason, a reader should check the context before accepting a synonym. The word large can replace big in many sentences, but not in every case.

When you read a paraphrase, ask whether it expresses the same claim as the original. If the claim changes, the paraphrase is incorrect even if it sounds smooth. Compare the main idea of both versions. If the main idea is identical, the paraphrase succeeds.

Paraphrasing also helps in speaking. When you explain a story to a friend, you naturally rephrase the parts you remember. In academic writing, however, you must cite the source. A paraphrase without a citation can still count as plagiarism, because the idea belongs to someone else.
